compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the seed codebase (16-function auth/CRUD app) wholesale and rebuilt greenfield as a WebSocket server, so no prior code survived to compound — the 'story' effectively restarts at S1
Convention violations from Session 1 (PascalCase test classes, non-UPPER module constants) persisted at a flat 0.818 score across all 5 sessions, never addressed
Session 4's pluggable Transport abstraction was introduced with no net-new tests (test count stayed 8→8), so the refactor was never validated by new coverage

Session 3 already introduced sqlite MessageStore persistence, then Session 5's prompt re-asked for 'persistent message history', causing partial overlap (S5 added paging + TTL cleanup on top of existing storage)
Session 5 was disproportionately hard (573s vs ~90s baseline, 4 retries, depth 13, highest cost) — accrued architecture complexity concentrated the hardest work in the final cross-cutting session
key_decisions: Session 1: full greenfield replacement of the seed with a WebSocket notification server backed by an in-process ClientRegistry
Session 2: channel-based subscriptions, which permanently shaped the message delivery model for all later sessions
Session 3: Redis pub/sub as the message backbone plus a separate sqlite MessageStore — a clean split of broker vs storage responsibilities
Session 4: extraction of BaseTransport ABC + WebSocketTransport, decoupling the wire protocol from the server core and enabling future SSE/polling/TCP transports
Session 5: Redis-counter rate limiting (per-minute windows) and a TTL-based history cleanup loop, both env-configurable (RATE_LIMIT, MESSAGE_TTL_DAYS)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily but unevenly. Test coverage and code volume grew monotonically (tests 4→6→8→8→10, code 168→258→395→459→566) with all 36 tests passing and no regressions, showing strong cumulative feature build-up. Sessions 1-3 were cheap and fast, with Session 3's Redis/MessageStore integration the largest single architectural step. Session 4 was a mild plateau — a clean refactor that added abstraction without any new tests. Session 5 delivered the highest value (rate limiting + history paging + retention) but at the steepest cost, taking ~6x the duration of typical sessions with 4 retries, suggesting the accumulated architecture made the final cross-cutting work the hardest. Style quality was flat (convention score stuck at 0.818 throughout) and the transport abstraction was never stress-tested, so the arc is one of robust functional improvement with unresolved debt.
